Replace unavailable units from a reserve list

Source: R/state.R
use_reserves.Rd

design_simple() and design_spread() with reserve give a list: the n units of the main sample, then the reserves, with a .reserve column that numbers them 1, 2, ... in the order they are used. Visit every unit of the main sample, and for each one found unavailable, visit the next reserve, until the units found available make up n. use_reserves() takes the list and what the visits found, and returns the sample to estimate from: the units of the main sample found available, and as many reserves, taken in order, as replace the others.

Usage

use_reserves(sample, unavailable)

Arguments

sample

A list from draw() with weights = TRUE and a design with reserve, or from as_drawn().

unavailable

A logical vector with one value for each row of sample, in its order, or the name of such a column of sample. See "Marking the visits".

Value

A weighted sample, ready for ht_total(), ht_mean(), as_svydesign() and sample_summary().

What the estimates describe

Replacing units changes the population being estimated. The sample that comes back stands for the units of the frame that can be reached, and its totals and means are theirs, not the whole frame's. It is weighted as a sample of n drawn at equal probability from the frame without the u listed units found unavailable: each unit used has probability n / (N - u), and the units found unavailable have probability 0, so ht_total() and ht_mean() count them among the frame rows the estimate does not cover.

The probabilities assume that every unit of the frame nobody visited is available. A frame that holds more unavailable units than were found has fewer than N - u units that can be reached, and the totals are too high by about the share of the frame those units make up. The Hajek mean of ht_mean() does not depend on N - u and is not affected. An estimate from the sample keeps u in unavailable, and its printed unreachable line adds that the units nobody visited are taken as available.

For design_simple() the weighting is exact under that assumption, when the reserves suffice. The list is one random draw in random order, so its first n available units are a simple random sample of n from the available units of the frame, and the variance is that of a simple random sample from N - u. For design_spread() the reserves are a second spread sample from the rows the main sample left, in random order. The units used are spread over the space, and under the same assumption their probabilities average n / (N - u), but each unit's own probability is not known exactly, so the weights are an approximation. The variance is the local mean estimator over the units used.

Reserves are for units that cannot be reached or measured at all. A unit that is reached but gives no answer is nonresponse: keep it in the sample with y missing, as "Missing values and nonresponse" in ht_total() describes.

Marking the visits

unavailable holds one value for each row of sample: TRUE for a unit found unavailable, FALSE for one found available, and NA for one not visited. Every unit of the main sample needs TRUE or FALSE, and so does each reserve up to the one that completes the sample; a missing value there is refused, with the frame row named. Reserves visited past that one are not used, and those of them found unavailable count among the u units outside the population. When the reserves run out first, the sample holds fewer than n units and is weighted as a sample of that many, with a warning.

What comes back

The units used, in the order of sample, with .prob, .weight, .row and .reserve first. .reserve is 0 for a unit of the main sample and the reserve's number for a unit that replaced one. The design stored with the result is the list's design with n the number of units used, no reserve, and the frame rows found unavailable recorded as unavailable; inclusion_prob() of it gives those rows probability 0.

See also

design_simple(), design_spread(), add_fieldwork() to add what the visits found to the list.

Examples

pop <- data.frame(id = 1:200, spend = (1:200) %% 37)
s <- draw(pop, design_simple(n = 20, reserve = 5), seed = 1, weights = TRUE)
table(s$.reserve)
#> 
#>  0  1  2  3  4  5 
#> 20  1  1  1  1  1 

# Two units of the main sample could not be reached, nor could the first
# reserve; reserves 2 and 3 replaced them, and 4 and 5 were not visited
gone <- c(s$id[c(3, 11)], s$id[s$.reserve == 1])
found <- ifelse(s$.reserve <= 3, s$id %in% gone, NA)
used <- use_reserves(s, found)
table(used$.reserve)
#> 
#>  0  2  3 
#> 18  1  1 
ht_total(used, "spend")
#> Horvitz-Thompson total  (simple design, n = 20)
#>   estimate 3,319.45
#>   se       514.6565  (analytic)
#>   95% CI  2,242.261 to 4,396.639  (t, 19 df)
#>   deff     1  (about the same as simple random sampling)
#>   unreachable  3 frame rows at probability 0, not covered by this estimate
#>                (3 found unavailable; rows not visited are taken as available)
